thread:
ana: Hey — sketching a small prototype for a "token variance" alert on the cost dashboard. Goal: detect when per-invocation token cost deviates from expected by > 40% for >5min and attribute to prefetch/cache hits failing.

mike: Sounds useful. Is this per-model or per-route?

ana: Per-route first, then roll up to per-model SKU. We need to show both the anomaly and a candidate cause (cache miss, model fallback, quant change).

sophia: Quick Q: how do we define 'expected'? rolling 24h median? moving percentile?

jared: moving 7d median + hourly smoothing probably ok. We have to exclude release windows and canary rollouts.

lina: If we trigger an alert, UX should link to: 1) sample invocations, 2) cached vs non-cached token breakdown, 3) rollout/traffic change history.

ana: Agreed. Proto wireframe: left: sparkline + alert banner; center: sample invocations table; right: breakdown pie (cache saved tokens vs direct tokens).

mike: For attribution, we can add a simple scorer: score = 0.6*cache_miss_rate_change + 0.3*avg_token_length_change + 0.1*model_sku_shift. If > threshold mark 'likely cache regression'.

sophia: Love that. Need to ensure we don't double-count prefetch credits. Also tie in cached KV fingerprint mismatch metric.

ops-bot: deployer: new metric "cache_prefetch_mismatch_rate" registered for prod.cluster-a at 2865432200

jared: Example query to surface candidates:
```
SELECT route, count(*) as invocations, avg(tokens) as avg_tokens,
  sum(case when cache_hit then 1 else 0 end) as hits
FROM invocations
WHERE ts > now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY invocations desc
LIMIT 50;
```

lina: UX ask: add a toggle to normalize by request size so tiny routes don't spam alerts.

ana: We also need a 'reconciliation panel' that shows prefetch credits applied vs consumed so billing matches the cache-savings card in console.

mike: Implementation-wise: metric pipeline emits both raw tokens and adjusted tokens after cache credits. Dashboard computes variance on adjusted_tokens.

sophia: Concern: this will add cardinality. Can we sample routes < 1 req/min and only aggregate? saves storage.

ana: yes — sample low-volume routes, full fidelity for top 5% traffic. We'll include sampling flags in the panel.

jared: Next steps: I can sketch the query set + alert rule, mike can wire the scoring, lina will mock the dashboard tiles. Can we aim for an internal demo next Thurs?

mike: thumbs up from me. @ana please drop the mock link when ready.

lina: will do. mock in Figma by Tue EOD.

ana: thanks all. logging an internal RFC in #eng-docs after we demo. :rocket:
